question: Animals where the fertilisation of eggs and the development of the baby up to the fetal stage takes place inside the mother's body are known as _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**viviparous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Animals that give birth to live young ones and where fertilization occurs internally are classified as **viviparous animals**.
 
• In viviparous animals, the embryo develops inside the mother’s body, and nourishment is provided through a placenta or other internal structures.
 
• Examples of viviparous animals include most mammals, such as humans, lions, and whales.
 
• Viviparity ensures better protection and survival chances for the offspring as they develop in a controlled internal environment.
 
• Viviparous reproduction is an advanced evolutionary adaptation compared to oviparity (egg-laying), as it increases the likelihood of offspring survival in challenging environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oviparous**

 
 
• Oviparous animals lay eggs, and the development of the embryo occurs outside the mother’s body.
 
• Fertilization can occur either internally (e.g., birds, reptiles) or externally (e.g., fish, amphibians).
 
• Examples include hens, frogs, snakes, and fish.
 
• Oviparity is common in species where external environmental factors provide suitable conditions for egg development.
 
 
 
• **Vertebrates**
 
 
• Vertebrates are animals that possess a backbone or spinal column.
 
• They belong to the phylum Chordata and include classes such as mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish.
 
• Both oviparous and viviparous animals can be vertebrates.
 
• Examples include humans, snakes, frogs, and sharks.
 
 
 
• **Invertebrates**
 
 
• Invertebrates are animals that lack a backbone or spinal column.
 
• This group includes animals such as insects, arachnids, mollusks, crustaceans, and sponges.
 
• Most invertebrates are oviparous, though there are some exceptions.
 
• Examples include octopuses, spiders, and jellyfish.
